key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over days to weeks. LOCATION: BILATERAL kidney involvement. DURATION: Develops over days to weeks, may persist for weeks to months. CHARACTER: HEMATURIA, proteinuria, swelling. AGGRAVATING: DEHYDRATION, medications. RELIEVING: IMMUNOSUPPRESSANTS, supportive care. TIMING: Gradual onset, develops over days to weeks. SEVERITY: 5-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: HEMATURIA, proteinuria, swelling, may have hypertension, may have decreased urine output. KEY POSITIVES: Hematuria, proteinuria, swelling, elevated creatinine, elevated BUN. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe fluid overload with respiratory distress - possible pulmonary edema, call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of uremia - confusion, seizures, coma - call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
